summary.reproduced: 332/332 run records reproduce byte-for-byte when applyGender is re-run on mt with the recorded settings and review-run.ts's two-name rule
summary.method: Every post-editor finding was re-run deterministically (scratchpad audit/build.ts calls applyGender and throws if the bad output does not reproduce). Lexicon claims were checked against the JSON and the cached dexonline pages; nothing was fetched.

postedit.title: Explicit he/she and lexically gendered subjects are overwritten by the speaker / anyone-else setting ('cea mai bună prietenă a mea' for 'He', 'profesor' for 'She', 'colegul meu' for 'His wife')
postedit.rootCause: Romanian is pro-drop, so the clause usually has no pronoun. analyze() only protects a span when the token directly before the copula is a Romanian pronoun (GENDERED_PRONOUN). The English he/she in `source` is never consulted, kinship subjects (Sora, Soția, fratele) are not recognised, and a name governs only when it is the token directly before the copula, so 'Maya, care este' and 'Josh crede că e' fall through to the anyone-else target.
postedit.location: src/ro/postedit.ts analyze() third() L185-186 + GENDERED_PRONOUN L138; targetFor() L363-367 falls back to 'other'
postedit.fix: Pin a clause's gender from the English subject (he/she, or a gendered kinship noun such as sister/wife/mother/brother/husband/father). Treat 'care este' after a name, and 'că e' after '<Name> <verb>', as that name's span.

postedit.title: 3rd-plural 'sunt' read as 'I am' ('Părinții mei sunt obosite', 'Copiii sunt fericite', and the pro-drop 'Sunt barmani' for 'They are')
postedit.rootCause: FIRST_PERSON contains 'sunt', which is also 3rd plural. The only guard is a pronoun or name directly before it, so a plural noun subject, or a dropped 'they', opens a speaker span.
postedit.fix: Treat 'sunt' as 1sg only when the English clause is 'I am/was' (the source is already passed in), or when it is clause-initial and not preceded by a plural or definite noun. Otherwise open an 'other' (3pl) span.

postedit.title: 1st-plural 'suntem' follows the speaker alone, so a mixed "we" becomes feminine ('Suntem fericite', 'suntem colege')
postedit.rootCause: 'suntem' is in FIRST_PERSON and opens a speaker span. Who is in the group (speaker plus husband; you and I) is ignored.

minimalRepro.mt: Tu și cu mine suntem obosiți.
minimalRepro.got: Tu și cu mine suntem obosite.
minimalRepro.expected: Tu și cu mine suntem obosiți.

postedit.fix: Give 'suntem'/'sunteți' a group span: feminine only when every known member is F (for 'tu și cu mine', the speaker and the addressee). Otherwise use masculine plural, or leave the MT output alone. A017 is the case where following the speaker is correct.

postedit.title: A possessive that agrees with a different noun gets flipped ('familia meu', 'echipa nostru', 'fratelui mea', 'fratele mea')
postedit.rootCause: The span runs to the end of the clause, and every indexed possessive inside it (meu/mea, nostru/noastră in FUNCTION_WORDS) is flipped. That includes possessives inside a prepositional phrase (din familia mea) or attached to a second noun (fratelui meu).
postedit.location: src/ro/postedit.ts analyze() L219 (span covers the rest of the clause); candidate loop L412-432; src/ro/words.ts FUNCTION_WORDS L64-67
postedit.fix: A possessive agrees with the noun it follows, so flip it only when that noun is itself a flipped candidate. Close the span at prepositions (din, de, la, în, cu, pentru) and after a genitive noun.

postedit.title: Article, possessive article or adjective flipped although the head noun cannot change ('o om', 'înaltă', 'o a 17-lea', 'o a XVII-lea', 'o Zorost', 'o welder')
postedit.rootCause: Every indexed token in the span is flipped on its own. 'un'/'o' and 'al'/'a' are indexed as function words, so they flip even when the noun they belong to has no counterpart: the epicene 'om', an MT non-word, an ordinal. The adjective then takes the wrong gender too ('înaltă').
postedit.location: src/ro/postedit.ts buildFormIndex() L62 (function words indexed unconditionally); candidate loop L412-432 (no head-noun check)
postedit.fix: Treat the noun phrase as a unit. Flip determiners, possessive articles and adjectives only when the head noun is itself flipped, or when the predicate has no noun at all ('Sunt obosit'). Never flip 'al' before an ordinal.

postedit.title: Noun flipped but its adjective left behind ('asistent medicală', and 'asistent/asistentă medicală' in both-forms mode)
postedit.rootCause: The MT renders 'nurse' as 'asistentă medicală'. 'medical/medicală' is in neither ADJECTIVES nor the lexicon, so only 'asistentă' changes. In both-forms mode the doublet covers only the noun.
postedit.location: src/ro/words.ts ADJECTIVES L9-16; lexicon index 46 (nurse) is single-word; src/ro/postedit.ts candidate loop L412-432
postedit.fix: Store nurse as the multiword pair 'asistent medical' / 'asistentă medicală', or add medical/medicală to ADJECTIVES. With P5's noun-phrase rule the adjective then follows its noun, including inside a doublet.

postedit.title: Only the first of several coordinated predicates is rewritten ('doctoriță și profesor', 'obosită și fericit', 'înaltă, obosit și fericit', 'o prietenă bună și un coleg bun')
postedit.rootCause: 'și' counts as a clause BOUNDARY unless it directly follows the copula, and any trailing comma closes the span. So the second and later items of the same predicate fall outside it. In both-forms mode the second variant is built from the same cut-off span (A210). With 'avoid', the cut produces a half paraphrase (B104).
postedit.location: src/ro/postedit.ts BOUNDARY L129-132; analyze() L212-217 and L220
postedit.fix: Keep the span open across 'și' and ',' when what follows is another predicate item (an article, adjective or noun candidate) and no new finite verb or subject comes in between. 'și eu sunt' still closes it.

postedit.title: The avoid-gender paraphrase drops modifiers and complements ('Predai.' for 'a good teacher', 'Predau.' for 'the best teacher', 'Tu editezi.' for 'the editor of this magazine')
postedit.rootCause: The paraphrase swaps the copula for the gender-free verb and deletes every token from copula+1 to the end of the span, whatever those tokens are ('bun', 'cel mai bun', 'acestei reviste'). It also paraphrases when the span holds a second noun that has no paraphrase.
postedit.location: src/ro/postedit.ts edit() avoid branch L393-410 (L409 deletes the whole span)

minimalRepro.expected: Ești un profesor bun/o profesoară bună. (doublet fallback) or 'Predai bine.'

postedit.fix: Paraphrase only when the span is exactly an optional [un/o] plus one paraphrasable occupation noun, plus punctuation. Otherwise set fellBack and print the doublet. Optionally map a lone 'bun' to 'bine'.

postedit.title: The subject noun before the copula is not rewritten for an unnamed third party ('Vecinul meu e grădinăreasă', 'Doctorul e o prietenă', 'Doctorul care este vecina mea')
postedit.rootCause: A span opens AT the copula, so the subject noun phrase to its left ('Vecinul meu', 'Doctorul') never belongs to it, and the sentence ends up with mixed genders. The reviewers labelled A076 'out-of-coverage', but 'vecin' is in NOUNS and 'Vecinul' is indexed.
postedit.location: src/ro/postedit.ts analyze() start() L168-173 (span begins at the copula)
postedit.fix: For a 3rd-person span with no name, also take in the definite subject noun phrase directly before the copula (the noun and its possessive), when that noun is indexed.

postedit.title: Coordinated named subjects never control a plural predicate, so all-female groups stay masculine ('Maya și Ana sunt colegii mei', 'Kim și Sam sunt programatori buni')
postedit.rootCause: When 'sunt' follows a name, analyze() just closes the span (open = undefined) instead of opening a span for the whole group of names.
postedit.fix: Open a group span for 'Name (, Name)* și Name sunt': feminine plural when every named target is F, masculine plural otherwise.

postedit.title: Definite (articled) forms are not rewritten for some lexicon words ('auditorul', 'procurorul', 'ministrul')
postedit.rootCause: buildFormIndex() indexes the 8 paradigm cells only when BOTH formsM and formsF exist. auditor has formsM = null; prosecutor and minister have formsF = null. So their definite forms are unknown to the post-editor. The bare lemma pair is still indexed, which is why A018, A139 and A096 work. This is a gap in the lexicon, not a bug in the span logic.
postedit.location: src/ro/postedit.ts buildFormIndex() L49 (both-paradigms condition); lexicon index 8, 44, 63
postedit.fix: Fill in the missing paradigms (the DOOM3-backed values are in the lexicon section). 16 entries have formsF = null and 3 have formsM = null; any of them can show this miss.

postedit.title: The hyphenated possessive article 'de-al' is never re-agreed ('o colegă de-al lui', 'o prietenă de-al mea')
postedit.rootCause: findGendered() splits on whitespace and looks up the whole token. 'de-al' is not in the index, so it never becomes a candidate.

minimalRepro.en: I am a colleague of his.

postedit.fix: Add the closed set de-al/de-a and de-ai/de-ale as function-word pairs.

postedit.title: 'ca' + occupation is only handled after a name ('Lucrez ca fotograf' stays masculine for a female speaker)
postedit.rootCause: The 'ca' rule needs a recognised name two tokens back. A 1sg/2sg verb (Lucrez/Lucrezi) or a kinship subject never opens a span.
postedit.fix: At 'ca', open a speaker/addressee span when the verb before it is 1sg/2sg (English 'I/you work as'), and an 'other' span after a kinship subject.

postedit.title: The clitic-fused perfect 'mi-a fost' is not recognised as a copula
postedit.rootCause: The PERFECT check compares the bare token with 'a'. 'mi-a' (likewise i-a, ți-a, ne-a) does not match, so no span opens.

minimalRepro.en: Maya has been a friend to me.

postedit.fix: Strip a leading dative clitic (mi-, ți-, i-, ne-, v-, le-) before the PERFECT lookup, and keep the name check on the token before it.

postedit.title: A name that ends one sentence blocks the 'Sunt' of the next sentence ('Eu sunt Ana. Sunt profesor.')
postedit.rootCause: The 'sunt after a name' guard reads prev = bare('Ana.') = 'ana' straight across the full stop, so the speaker's next sentence is taken as 3rd plural.

minimalRepro.en: I am Ana. I am tired.

postedit.fix: Treat prev as empty when the previous raw token ends in . ! or ?

postedit.title: The object clitic is not re-agreed after its noun changes ('profesoară pe care-l am')
postedit.rootCause: Clitic pronouns (-l / o) are not modelled.

minimalRepro.en: You are the best teacher I have.
minimalRepro.mt: Ești cel mai bun profesor pe care-l am.
minimalRepro.got: Ești cea mai bună profesoară pe care-l am.
minimalRepro.expected: Ești cea mai bună profesoară pe care o am.

postedit.fix: Add 'pe care-l' -> 'pe care o' (and the plurals -i / le) when the noun before it was flipped.

postedit.title: Once two people are named, the anyone-else row is dropped, so unnamed third parties ('șeful', 'vecinul', 'regizorul') cannot be set
postedit.rootCause: This is UI design, not the post-editor: run() re-applies the edit with addressee = undefined when people.length >= 2, and the eval harness does the same. The intents of B047-B049 expect the row to keep applying to unnamed people. Turning it back on would expose P6 ('asistent medicală' in B048) and P9 ('șeful meu e fericită' in B047, where 'șeful' is not indexed at all).

minimalRepro.en: Ana is tired, Mihai is tired and my neighbour is tired.
minimalRepro.mt: Ana e obosită, Mihai e obosit și vecinul meu e obosit.
minimalRepro.got: Ana e obosită, Mihai e obosit și vecinul meu e obosit.  (main.ts / review-run drop the row; calling applyGender directly gives "... vecinul meu e obosită", i.e. P9)
minimalRepro.expected: Ana e obosită, Mihai e obosit și vecina mea e obosită.

postedit.fix: Keep the anyone-else row while the sentence still has unnamed 3rd-person spans (othersGuess is defined), and hide it only when every span belongs to a named person.

postedit.title: Half-correction when the head noun is unknown ('Suntem sportivi obosite')
postedit.rootCause: The adjective is indexed and flipped, but its noun ('sportivi') is not in the lexicon, which leaves a mixed predicate. This is the same missing noun-phrase check as P5.

minimalRepro.expected: Suntem sportivi obosiți. (leave untouched until 'sportiv' is covered) or 'Suntem sportive obosite.'

postedit.fix: The P5 rule covers it: do not flip an adjective that follows an unknown noun. Also add sportiv/sportivă to coverage.

flags.title: The masculine 'inginer' carries the "contested" flag
flags.rootCause: addPair() attaches the entry's status and note to BOTH readings of a pair, the masculine and the feminine. The status describes only the feminine (see the GenderedForm.status doc comment and lexicon.ts realize() L251-256, which returns 'normative' for the masculine). The UI (main.ts render() L120-122, collectNotes() L142-147) and the eval harness (review-run.ts L51) read options[0].status without checking agreement. So the bug starts in the post-editor's data and shows up in the UI. Across all 332 runs, the only masculine forms that got flagged are these 5 'inginer' tokens.
flags.location: src/ro/postedit.ts addPair() L29-41, called at L48/L51 with e.status/e.note; src/ui/main.ts L120-122
flags.fix: In addPair(), put status and note only on the F reading (or leave them undefined for agreement 'M'). That one change fixes the UI and the harness.

flags.title: 'radioloagă' is not flagged although DOOM3 lists radiologă (livr.) / radioloagă (colocv.)
flags.rootCause: Lexicon index 65 has status 'attested', f = 'radioloagă' and fAlt = null, so the flag (variant/contested only) never fires. Its siblings psiholog and zoolog are 'variant'.
flags.fix: Set f = 'radiologă', fAlt = 'radioloagă', status = 'variant' (see lexicon index 65).

flags.title: 'designeră' has no flag (both sentence reviewers marked the flag as missing)
flags.rootCause: Index 24 has status 'attested', and 'attested' is never flagged. The reviewers disagree on whether the word is settled: sentence reviewer y calls it rare/contested, while lexicon reviewer 1 says DOOM3 added '+designeră' unmarked, which would make it normative. The dexonline cache for designeră is empty (0-byte file), so neither claim is grounded.
flags.location: src/ro/lexicon.occupations.json index 24; src/ui/main.ts L120-122 (only variant/contested are shown)

flags.rootCause: Index 44 has formsF = null, so the definite forms are not indexed (P11), and the contested note is never reached. In register terms the output is defensible: DOOM3 marks ministră (fam.) (colocv.).
flags.fix: Fill formsF for minister. Then decide whether a contested word should be rewritten at all, or kept masculine and flagged.

flags.title: 'medică' is flagged contested, but the note should say DOOM3 does not sanction it as a noun
flags.rootCause: The flag fires correctly, but the note ('kaikki records medică; doamna doctor competes') misstates the evidence: DOOM3 has medic² s.m. only, and 'medică' only as the feminine of the adjective medic¹ (math., 'median'). Both sentence reviewers accepted 'Sunt medică', so they disagree with the lexicon reviewer, and the cache supports the lexicon reviewer.
flags.fix: Rewrite the note (lexicon index 53). Consider not rewriting medic to medică at all.

mt.description: The MT produced a non-word, an untranslated English word or the wrong lexeme for the occupation ('archivistul', 'librarian', 'librarianul', 'preot' for minister, 'al 17-lea' for plumber, 'sai' for sailor, 'inspector' for surveyor, 'welder', 'Zorost'). Acord left these unchanged, and nothing in Acord can repair them.

The same kind of MT garbage, but Acord made it worse by flipping 'un'/'al' onto it ('o a 17-lea', 'o Zorost'). The Acord part is P5, so these appear there as well. The y reviewer's 'mt' attribution is only half right.
'director' was translated as 'regizorul' (film director). The gender part could not be set because of P17.

The MT put a masculine (or, in B041, feminine) form against an explicit or kinship subject ('Sora mea este un coleg', 'Sora mea lucrează ca chelner', 'Lucrează ca asistentă' for 'He', 'Sora ta este, de asemenea, un doctor'). Acord did not cause these; it left the MT form alone. It could fix them only through P1/P13 (English pronoun and kinship-subject detection). B064's 'un doctor' for a woman is awkward rather than wrong.
'un prieten care este asistentă medicală' mixes genders for one person. The intent is to leave it, and Acord did. This is an MT inconsistency.
The MT gave the feminine 'recepționistă' to a male speaker. Acord cannot correct it because the lexicon holds recepționer/recepționeră, not recepționist(ă) (see coverage).
